findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. On this alone they could say what it is and why it matters.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The title and heading are about a different project, firstmate, not about Athena. Someone who came to the Athena site has to read the lede to learn that this page is a demonstration and not Athena's own documentation.
findings.source:
/

Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: A link near the top jumps straight to the next steps, so a newcomer does not have to scroll through the long firstmate study to find out how to start.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The next steps give a concrete path: what to install first, the clone command, the setup script and a one-line first request. That is enough to try Athena.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page promises a traceable commit with a cost and a verdict, but nothing on it shows one. The whole demonstration is a code-reading study, so a newcomer sees no example of Athena's core output: a commit with its request, models, cost and verdict. The page also never names the second, checking model.
findings.source: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: This link speaks to the site owner ("your decision") and appears in the header a newcomer reads first, where it is likely to confuse them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state-machine study of firstmate, with exit codes, guards and 44 claims. A newcomer who wants Athena is unlikely to read it, though its claim-to-source links do show the traceability that the lede promises.
findings.source: Headings "Start here", "States of a piece of work", "Transitions", "Counters", "Claims and sources"

findings.text: This section describes repository internals that mean nothing to a first-time visitor who has not cloned anything.
